VERIDANE - INTERNAL - Product Safety Committee memo PSC-2026-07
Date: 2 Oct 2026     From: Elena Kowalczyk, VP Quality & Product Safety     To: Executive Leadership Team

Subject: GV-400 series combination gas valve - voluntary recall (CPSC Fast Track)

Summary
- Affected units: ~41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves, date codes 2507-2612, sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters.
- Issue: diaphragm seat can deform under sustained high-inlet-pressure conditions, allowing gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. 17 field reports of gas odor; 2 reports of delayed ignition causing cabinet damage; no injuries reported.
- Root cause: change of diaphragm compound supplier (Q1 2025); supplier lot material out of spec on compression set. Corrective action complete; replacement valves shipping from Mequon plant since 28 Sep.
- Regulatory: CPSC Fast Track filed 22 Sep; joint recall notice expected the week of 19 Oct. Canada (Health Canada) notification filed.
- Cost: reserve booked in Q3 $21.6M (field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement, logistics). Range $18-26M. Supplier recovery claim of ~$9M lodged, not recognised.
- Customer impact: three OEMs (incl. our 2nd-largest BCV customer) have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice. Included in updated guidance.

For release: Thursday, 5 November 2026, 4:05 p.m. ET

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

The third quarter showed both engines of this company at work. Thermal & Data Center Solutions, our data-center cooling business, grew net sales 13.4% year over year, we won two new hyperscale awards, and our data-center backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0%. Net sales for the quarter were $412.6 million, adjusted EBITDA was $48.7 million (an 11.8% margin), and adjusted EPS was $0.15. The key metrics for the quarter are set out in the accompanying KPI table.

## Highlights
- Two new hyperscale awards in Q3; record data-center cooling backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year, and total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Thermal & Data Center Solutions net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, led by liquid cooling demand and the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger ramp.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million; adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- Completed a voluntary, proactive, customer-first recall of certain GV-400 series gas valves with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) under its Fast Track program; corrective action is complete and replacement valves began shipping in late September.
- Launched Project Keystone, a company-wide cost and efficiency program targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC).** Net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% from $137.8 million a year ago. Demand for our cooling solutions continues to accelerate with rising rack densities and the industry's shift toward liquid cooling. In the quarter we were awarded two new hyperscale programs, and the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger introduced last quarter is now ramping with hyperscale customers. TDC backlog ended the quarter at $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year — a record, and a strong foundation for growth into FY2027.

**Building Controls & Valves (BCV).** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% from $301.2 million, reflecting the continued softness in commercial construction that we flagged earlier in the year and more cautious ordering from OEM customers.

In September, we initiated a voluntary recall of certain GV-400 series combination gas valves, working with the CPSC under its Fast Track program. This was a proactive, customer-first decision: we identified the root cause — a supplier material issue — completed corrective action, and began shipping replacement valves from our Mequon facility in late September. We recorded a $21.6 million charge in the quarter to cover field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics. Several OEM customers paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice, and that pause is reflected in our updated guidance below. Together with the $6.2 million of Project Keystone restructuring charges recorded in the quarter, these items produced a net loss on a GAAP basis; the accompanying KPI table presents both GAAP and adjusted figures.

## Outlook

We are updating our FY2026 outlook to reflect the softer BCV market, the temporary pause in GV-400 orders, and the timing of data-center backlog conversion. We now expect FY2026 net sales of $1.66-1.70 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $205-215 million.

Backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0%, gives us unusual visibility, and the two hyperscale awards begin contributing to revenue over the next several quarters and build through FY2027. Project Keystone is moving quickly: actions across procurement, manufacturing footprint and overhead are underway, and we expect $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027. As GV-400 orders resume with the recall notice published and remediation complete, we expect BCV to stabilize.

We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash and are managing working capital closely as backlog converts to revenue.

## Closing

We want to thank our 6,200 employees, especially the quality, engineering and plant teams in Mequon whose rapid work made the recall response one of the fastest in our industry's history, and our customers for their partnership and trust. The quarter showed the resilience of our strategy: a fast-growing data-center franchise, a disciplined cost program, and a team that puts customers first. We appreciate your continued support.

Dana Whitcombe, President & Chief Executive Officer

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

The third quarter showed both engines of this company at work. ## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC).** Net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% from $137.8 million a year ago. Demand for our cooling solutions continues to accelerate with rising rack densities and the industry's shift toward liquid cooling. In the quarter we were awarded two new hyperscale programs, and the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger introduced last quarter is now ramping with hyperscale customers. TDC backlog ended the quarter at $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year — a record, and a strong foundation for growth into FY2027.

**Building Controls & Valves (BCV).** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% from $301.2 million, reflecting the continued softness in commercial construction that we flagged earlier in the year and more cautious ordering from OEM customers.

{"content":"# Veridane Fluid Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: VRDF) - Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders
(For release Thursday, 5 November 2026, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Data-center momentum defined our third quarter. Thermal & Data Center Solutions, our data-center cooling business, grew net sales 13.4% year over year, we won two new hyperscale awards, and our data-center backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0%. Core commercial HVAC stayed soft, and we moved quickly and decisively on a voluntary recall in our gas valve line. Net sales for the quarter were $412.6 million, adjusted EBITDA was $48.7 million (an 11.8% margin), and adjusted EPS was $0.15. The key metrics for the quarter, including GAAP figures, are set out in the accompanying KPI table.

## Highlights

- Two new hyperscale awards in Q3 and a record data-center cooling backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year; total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Thermal & Data Center Solutions net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, led by liquid-cooling demand and the ramp of the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million; adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- Completed a voluntary, proactive, customer-first recall of certain GV-400 series gas valves with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) under its Fast Track program; corrective action is complete and replacement valves began shipping in late September.
- Launched Project Keystone, a company-wide cost and efficiency program targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC).** Net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% from $137.8 million a year ago. Rising rack densities and the industry's shift toward liquid cooling continue to drive demand for our portfolio. In the quarter we were awarded two new hyperscale programs, and the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger introduced in Q2 is now ramping with hyperscale customers. TDC backlog ended the quarter at $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year - a record for the segment and a strong foundation for growth into FY2027. We continue to invest in assembly and test capacity ahead of this ramp, within our planned capital envelope.

**Building Controls & Valves (BCV).** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% from $301.2 million a year ago, reflecting the soft commercial construction activity we have described in recent quarters and more cautious ordering from OEM customers. Even so, BCV backlog held essentially flat year over year at $343.8 million.

In September, we initiated a voluntary recall of certain GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters, working with the CPSC under its Fast Track program. This was a proactive, customer-first decision. We identified the root cause - a supplier material issue - completed corrective action, and began shipping replacement valves from our Mequon facility in late September. We recorded a $21.6 million charge in the quarter to cover field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics. Several OEM customers paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice, and that pause is reflected in our updated guidance below. Together with the $6.2 million of Project Keystone restructuring charges recorded in the quarter, these items produced a net loss on a GAAP basis; the accompanying KPI table presents GAAP and adjusted results side by side.

## Outlook

We are updating our FY2026 outlook to reflect the softer BCV market, the temporary pause in GV-400 orders, and the timing of data-center backlog conversion. We now expect FY2026 net sales of $1.66-1.70 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $205-215 million.

The most important number in this quarter is backlog. At $918.0 million, up 13.0% year over year, it gives us visibility that few industrial companies enjoy. The two hyperscale awards begin contributing to revenue over the next several quarters and build through FY2027, and BCV backlog has stabilized. Project Keystone is moving quickly: actions across procurement, manufacturing footprint and overhead are underway, and we expect $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027, with benefits beginning to build through the balance of the fiscal year. With the recall notice now published and remediation complete, we expect GV-400 orders to resume, easing the pause at our BCV customers. The building blocks for FY2027 - a record data-center backlog, recovering GV-400 volumes and Keystone savings - are already visible.

We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash and are managing working capital closely as backlog converts to revenue.

## Closing

We want to thank our 6,200 employees - especially the quality, engineering and Mequon plant teams whose rapid work made this recall response among the fastest in our industry - and our customers for their partnership and trust. A fast-growing data-center franchise, a disciplined cost program and a team that puts customers first: that is the Veridane of this quarter, and the one you should expect next year. We appreciate your continued support.

Sincerely,

Dana Whitcombe, President & Chief Executive Officer

Mark Ostrander, EVP & Chief Financial Officer

# Veridane Fluid Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: VRDF) - Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders
(For release Thursday, 5 November 2026, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Data-center momentum defined our third quarter. Thermal & Data Center Solutions, our data-center cooling business, grew net sales 13.4% year over year, we won two new hyperscale awards, and our data-center backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0%. Core commercial HVAC stayed soft, and we moved quickly and decisively on a voluntary recall in our gas valve line. Net sales for the quarter were $412.6 million, adjusted EBITDA was $48.7 million (an 11.8% margin), and adjusted EPS was $0.15. The key metrics for the quarter, including GAAP figures, are set out in the accompanying KPI table.

## Highlights

- Two new hyperscale awards in Q3 and a record data-center cooling backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year; total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Thermal & Data Center Solutions net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, led by liquid-cooling demand and the ramp of the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million; adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- Completed a voluntary, proactive, customer-first recall of certain GV-400 series gas valves with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) under its Fast Track program; corrective action is complete and replacement valves began shipping in late September.
- Launched Project Keystone, a company-wide cost and efficiency program targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC).** Net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% from $137.8 million a year ago. Rising rack densities and the industry's shift toward liquid cooling continue to drive demand for our portfolio. In the quarter we were awarded two new hyperscale programs, and the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger introduced in Q2 is now ramping with hyperscale customers. TDC backlog ended the quarter at $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year - a record for the segment and a strong foundation for growth into FY2027. Conversion of the quarter's awards begins in the coming quarters and builds through FY2027. We continue to invest in assembly and test capacity ahead of this ramp, within our planned capital envelope.

**Building Controls & Valves (BCV).** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% from $301.2 million a year ago, reflecting the soft commercial construction activity we have described in recent quarters and more cautious ordering from OEM customers. Even so, BCV backlog held essentially flat year over year at $343.8 million.

In September, we initiated a voluntary recall of certain GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters, working with the CPSC under its Fast Track program. This was a proactive, customer-first decision. We identified the root cause - a supplier material issue - completed corrective action, and began shipping replacement valves from our Mequon facility in late September, and we are supporting OEM customers through the replacement process. We recorded a $21.6 million charge in the quarter to cover field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics. Several OEM customers paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice, and that pause is reflected in our updated guidance below.
